title.narrative: Freedom of expression, Council of Europe
Freedom of expression, Council of Europe

description.narrative: Det föreslagna projektets övergripande mål är att: Säkerställa att rätten till yttrandefrihet och rätten till informationsfrihet respekteras, skyddas och uppfylls, utan diskriminering, i Bosnien och Hercegovina. Del 1 kommer att behandla temat yttrandefrihet/mediefrihet med särskilt fokus på hatpropaganda. Komponentens fokus ligger på att förbättra effekten av MHRR. Del 2 kommer att behandla temat informationsfrihet/tillgång till information. Del 3 kommer att behandla samordningen av MHRR i allmänhet med tanke på mandatet för mänskliga rättigheter.

The overall objective of the proposed project is to: Ensure that the right to freedom of expression and the right to freedom of information are respected, protected and fulfilled, without discrimination, in Bosnia and Herzegovina. Component 1 will deal with the theme of freedom of expression / freedom of the media with a special focus on hate propaganda. The component's focus is on improving the effect of MHRR. Component 2 will deal with the theme of freedom of information / access to information. Component 3 will address the coordination of the MHRR in general with a view to the mandate for human rights.

The proposed action builds on past and current CoE activities in the area of Freedom of Access to Information/Media and Freedom of Expression in BiH, including a Sida-funded pilot project implemented in 2019/2020 (extended due to COVID-19). The proposed project has three inter-connected components: 1) Freedom of Expression (with a specific focus on Hate Speech); 2) Freedom of Access to Information; and 3) Capacity-building of the MHRR to enhance its mandate . The objectives of the projects are to contribute to ensuring a human rights-based legal framework and practice, by enhancing the capacity of key duty-bearers (principally the MHRR) and rights-holder representatives (including media actors and CSOs) to integrate a human rights-based approach in their work (including awareness-raising; legislative analysis; capacity-building; monitoring, advocacy and reporting). The Theory of Change of the project is that effective implementation of a human rights-based legislative framework on Freedom of Expression and Freedom of Information is critical for BiHs progress as a Rule of Law state. Reflecting the interdependence of human rights, vindicating the rights to FoE/FoI is dependent on respect for a range of other human rights, including participation, assembly, education, etc. In turn, the human rights to FoE/FoI are critical for other rights to be guaranteed, including participation in public life; free and fair elections; conscience/religion; privacy; access to justice etc. The right to equality and non-discrimination is a cross-cutting legal entitlement. A central premise of the project is that enhanced capacity/systems for full-cycle (see below) FoE/FoI monitoring will provide a foundation for enhanced MHRR delivery of its mandate with regard to the full spectrum of human rights. The proposed projects overall objective (impact) is to: Ensure that the right to freedom of expression and the right to freedom of information is respected, protected and fulfilled, without discrimination, in BiH.
Specific objectives (intermediate outcomes) are: i)Enhanced effectiveness of the MHRR and other key actors in BiH to address freedom of expression/media (in particular hate speech). Aiming at enhancing substantive awareness/knowledge and methodological skills/capacity to implement the full cycle of human rights monitoring - from information gathering, human rights gap analysis/needs assessment, through to design/delivery of action for change (legislative drafting, awareness-raising/training, development of guidelines/tools, domestic/international reporting, advocacy, etc).
ii)Enhanced effectiveness of the MHRR and other key actors in BiH to address freedom of information, Aiming at enhancing substantive awareness/knowledge and methodological skills/capacity to implement the full cycle of human rights monitoring - from information gathering, human rights gap analysis/needs assessment, through to design/delivery of action for change (legislative drafting, awareness-raising/advocacy, domestic/international reporting, etc).
iii)Enhanced organisational management capacity of the MHRR as a key duty-bearer institution to apply a human rights-based approach in the execution of its mandate (aiming at project management, coordination of FoE/FoI monitoring and information sharing/liaison with relevant domestic and international actors).

sector.narrative: Media and free flow of information

description.narrative:
Sida has assessed that the intervention has generated significant institutional and policy-level changes in the area of freedom of expression (FoE) and access to information (FoI) in Bosnia and Herzegovina. The most important achievement is the strengthening of the role and capacity of the Ministry of Human Rights and Refugees (MHRR) as the lead institution responsible for co-ordinating monitoring, reporting, and policy development related to FoE and FoI. The Ministry moved from being a participant in the process to assuming a leadership role in inter-institutional co-operation, monitoring and reporting, and engagement with international human rights mechanisms. The reports submitted are covering the period from 01.02.2022. - 31.12.2025.
A particularly important result is the establishment and institutionalisation of the Cross-Co-ordinating Working Group, bringing together 14 institutions, independent bodies, and civil society organisations. This is the first formal mechanism in Bosnia and Herzegovina dedicated to collaborative, human-rights-based monitoring and reporting on freedom of expression and access to information. Beyond the project period, the Working Group is expected to continue functioning as a permanent platform for dialogue, evidence gathering, and policy development.
The project also resulted in the preparation of the first collaborative Pilot Report on Freedom of Expression and Access to Information in Bosnia and Herzegovina. This represents a systemic change rather than a one-off output, as it establishes a baseline and methodology for future national monitoring and reporting while strengthening institutional ownership within the MHRR and other participating institutions.
In the field of freedom of information, institutional capacities have improved substantially. Public officials, information officers, independent institutions, and civil society representatives increased their knowledge of international standards, including the Tromsø Convention (Council of Europe treaty guaranteeing public access to official documents and government information), access-to-information procedures, and the balance between transparency and data protection. The introduction of simplified data collection tools and reporting methodologies has contributed to more systematic and sustainable monitoring practices.
Another important sustainability result is the development and institutional ownership of an online course on access to information, hosted by the Civil Service Agency of Bosnia and Herzegovina. Because the course remains publicly available and under domestic institutional ownership, it creates long-term opportunities for continued capacity development beyond the life of the project.
The project contributed to strengthening institutional responses to threats against media freedom and journalist safety. The Working Group was transformed into Bosnia and Herzegovinas national committee under the Council of Europes Journalists Matter initiative, creating structured co-operation among government institutions, prosecutors, police, civil society organisations, and journalists. This process has already contributed to the preparation of the countrys first national strategic framework and action plan on journalist safety.
The project also influenced policy discussions related to defamation, hate speech, and Strategic Lawsuits Against Public Participation (SLAPPs). Through legal analyses, guidance documents, and stakeholder dialogue, institutions and civil society actors gained access to practical tools and European standards that can inform future legislative and policy reforms. This is particularly relevant given the challenging environment following the re-criminalisation of defamation in Republika Srpska.
An unexpected but highly significant result was the role played by the MHRR in leading Bosnia and Herzegovinas accession to the Council of Europe Framework Convention on Artificial Intelligence and Human Rights, Democracy and the Rule of Law. While AI governance was not among the projects original core objectives, the strengthened institutional capacity and policy engagement fostered by the project enabled the Ministry to take a leading role in this process. Bosnia and Herzegovina thereby became one of the early signatories of the first legally binding international framework on human-rights-based AI governance.
Another notable and partly unexpected result concerns the quality of co-operation established between institutions and civil society organisations. During the Project Steering Committee meeting, stakeholders highlighted the Working Group as evidence that meaningful and sustainable co-operation between public institutions and civil society is possible and effective. Civil society representatives specifically noted that the mechanism created new opportunities to raise issues and influence policy discussions that had previously not been addressed in a structured manner.
Overall, the intervention has produced sustainable institutional changes that go beyond individual trainings or project activities. The most important outcomes include strengthened state ownership of freedom of expression and access-to-information monitoring, improved institutional co-operation, enhanced protection mechanisms for journalists, improved reporting methodologies, and stronger alignment with European and Council of Europe standards.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
